## Window
Round 1, the final round and the post-mortem for the run. Window 2026-10-15T21:38:40 to 2026-10-16T02:05:11 (+01:00), though all board activity is in seqs 1–27, about 21:39–21:41. Live now: 0 solvers and 0 supervisors (I am the only supervisor). No knob had been tuned before this round. There is no previous window to compare against.

## Succession
- 4 handoff requests, 3 real handoffs (for example seq 22 from sol-001), 2 stubs, 2 kills.
- Handoff success rate is 0.6 (n=5), with no baseline. Median time from request to handoff was 5.64 s.
- No earlier tune to evaluate.
- Lineages L-002 and L-003 reached generation 3 and L-001 generation 2. For a pack of 8 tasks finished in about 2 minutes, that is churn: each solver burned through its context in only a few tasks.
- The stub successors did not redo work: duplicate_rate is 0 (n=7). sol-003-g3 finished T-007 by building on seqs 12–20.

## Queue and SLOs
- Tasks: 8 done, 0 open, 0 leased, 0 blocked. Verifier mean score 0.946.
- SLOs, all first-window values:
  - completions_per_mtok 2.73 (n=8)
  - blocked_failed_rate 0 (n=8)
  - duplicate_rate 0 (n=7)
  - lease_wait_median_s 15.4 (n=8)
  - handoff_success_rate 0.6 (n=5)
- Lowest scores:
  - T-005 scored 0.667. years_between was 1 where 2 was expected (seq 17/20, corrected at seq 21).
  - T-007 scored 0.9; it was missing the "michaelmas" keyword. "Michaelmas" appeared in seq 17, but the chronicle (seq 26) left it out.
- Throughput and queue health were good. Succession was the only weak SLO.

## Actions taken
- Votes:
  - +1 on seq 21: the correct years_between convention.
  - −1 on seq 17: its convention was scored wrong.
  - +1 on seq 22: an exemplary handoff.
  - All three returned weight 0 because no solvers are live. They are a record only.
- No tune. Solvers are gone, any tune would expire at its TTL before another solver ran, and there is no previous window for hysteresis. Had solvers been live, I would have lowered handoff_pct from 80 to 70 (slo handoff_success_rate, 2 kills of 5 successions).
- No blockers, alerts or reopens. No ping: the succession_failing trigger needs kills in two windows, and only one exists.

## Diagnosis
- **sol-003 (L-003 gen 1, T-007):** I confirm no_chance, with a note. The request landed at 87% context, and the kill came 2.72 s later with zero turns and zero tool calls in between. The next turn crossed kill_pct before the agent could act. The root cause is the same as never_asked: one turn can add more than the gap between handoff_pct and kill_pct. The request arrived when the agent was already at 87%, not at about 80%.
- **sol-002 (L-002 gen 1, T-008):** I confirm never_asked. No request was ever sent; a single turn jumped from under 80% to over kill_pct.
- Together the two kills are a pattern: on this workload, single turns grow context by more than the handoff-to-kill gap, probably because whole materials files are read in one turn.
- Recommendations for the next run:
  1. Seed handoff_pct at 70 instead of 80. This addresses both kills.
  2. Consider kill_grace_turns 3.
  3. In the solver prompt, tell agents to read large materials with offset/limit rather than whole files.
- **Pack and verifier:**
  - T-005 does not say how to count years_between. The verifier wants calendar-year subtraction (2), and a careful solver reasonably computed complete years (1). Next run's task text should say "1855 minus 1853" or "calendar-year difference".
  - T-007's grader wants the word "michaelmas", which the task text never asks for. Either say "give the reopening date as the source names it" or drop that keyword group.
- The handoff prompt worked: seq 22 has every heading and is useful. The successes were not limited by prompt quality.

## For the operator
- The run succeeded: 8 of 8 done, mean 0.946, no blocked tasks, no duplicates.
- Two items to consider at leisure:
  1. Seed handoff_pct at 70 next run (2 kills of 5 successions; both kills came from a single turn jumping past the gap between handoff_pct and kill_pct).
  2. Fix the ambiguous task text for T-005 years_between and T-007 "michaelmas".
- Votes cast after the solvers have exited carry zero weight. If supervisor votes in a final round are meant to shape the next run's board, that is a harness design question.
- No ping sent.

## Window
This is round 2, the final round, so this report is the run's post-mortem. The window runs from 2026-10-15T21:38:40 to 2026-10-16T02:05:49 (+01:00). It starts at the same moment as round 1's window, and the board has nothing new since round 1's report (seq 28). Every board event in this window is one round 1 already counted, in seqs 1–27, roughly 21:39–21:41. 0 solvers and 0 supervisors are live; I am the only supervisor. No knob was tuned in either round.

## Succession
- 4 handoff requests, 3 real handoffs (seqs 22, 23, 24), 2 stubs, 2 kills.
- Handoff success rate is 0.6 (n=5), the same as last window (0.6, n=5). These are the same 5 successions counted twice, not a second bad window.
- No earlier tune to judge.
- Lineages L-002 and L-003 reached generation 3 and L-001 reached generation 2, all within about 2 minutes on an 8-task pack. That is churn.
- Stub successors (sol-002-g2/g3, sol-003-g2/g3) did not redo work: duplicate_rate is 0 (n=7), and seq 26 builds on seqs 12–20.

## Queue and SLOs
- Tasks: 8 done, 0 open, 0 leased, 0 blocked. Verifier mean score 0.946.
- SLOs, this window against the previous one:
  - completions_per_mtok 2.53 against 2.73 (n=8). The dip probably comes from tokens counted after the work ended, since the token rate was still 229k/min with no agents live. It is not a change in solver output.
  - blocked_failed_rate 0 against 0 (n=8).
  - duplicate_rate 0 against 0 (n=7).
  - lease_wait_median_s 15.4 against 15.4 (n=8).
  - handoff_success_rate 0.6 against 0.6 (n=5).
- Lowest scores: T-005 at 0.667 (years_between) and T-007 at 0.9 (missing the "michaelmas" keyword).

## Actions taken
- No tune. No agents are live, so a tune would expire at its TTL without affecting anyone, and the second window holds no new observations.
- No replies or reopens: there are no blockers, no blocked tasks and no alerts.
- No new votes. Nothing has been posted since seq 28, and round 1 already voted on seqs 17, 21 and 22. Those votes carried zero weight because no solvers were live.
- No ping. The succession_failing trigger (kills in this window and the previous one) may pass the server's check as written, but both windows hold the same two kills. Pinging on that would be double counting, not a sign that succession failed again after a tune.

## Diagnosis
**Incidents.** I agree with round 1's reading of both kills.
- sol-002, T-008: I confirm never_asked. No request was ever sent, and a single turn took the context from under 80% to over kill_pct.
- sol-003, T-007: I confirm no_chance, but it has the same root cause as sol-002. The request landed with context already at 87%, and the kill followed 2.72 s later with no turns and no tool calls in between.
- Together they show one thing: on this workload a single turn can add more context than the gap between handoff_pct and kill_pct.

**Next run: knobs**
1. Seed handoff_pct at 70 instead of 80. This addresses both kills.
2. Optionally set kill_grace_turns to 3. It only helps if the request lands early enough to use the extra turns.
3. Leave the other knobs at their seeds. The queue, duplicate and lease SLOs were all healthy.

**Next run: prompts**
- Tell solvers to read large materials files in parts (offset/limit), so that no single turn jumps past the gap.
- The handoff prompt is fine: seq 22 is a model handoff.

**Next run: pack**
- T-005: state the years_between convention, i.e. calendar-year difference 1855−1853=2 (see seqs 17, 20, 21).
- T-007: either ask for the reopening date "as the source names it" or drop the "michaelmas" keyword group.

**Next run: harness**
- A final round's window should start where the previous window ended. Otherwise the same incidents are counted twice, SLO history shows flat lines that are really duplicates, and succession_failing can be met by a single incident set.

## For the operator
- The run succeeded: 8 of 8 tasks done, mean score 0.946, no blocked tasks, no duplicates. The one weak point was succession, at 0.6 (2 kills).
- Recommendations at leisure: seed handoff_pct at 70, fix the T-005 and T-007 task text, and stop round windows from overlapping.
- Votes cast after the solvers have exited carry zero weight.
- No ping sent this round.
